Change c0464. Location: 1818 Vol. III, Ch. VI; 1831 Ch. XXIII.

Context before (unchanged): My father and Ernest yet lived; but the former sunk under the tidings that I bore.

1818 text: I see him now, excellent and venerable old man! his eyes wandered in vacancy, for they had lost their charm and their delight—his niece, his more than daughter, whom he doated on with all that affection which a man feels, who, in the decline of life, having few affections, clings more earnestly to those that remain.

1831 text: I see him now, excellent and venerable old man! his eyes wandered in vacancy, for they had lost their charm and their delight—his Elizabeth, his more than daughter, whom he doated on with all that affection which a man feels, who in the decline of life, having few affections, clings more earnestly to those that remain.

Diff: I see him now, excellent and venerable old man! his eyes wandered in vacancy, for they had lost their charm and their delight—his [-niece-] {+Elizabeth+} , his more than daughter, whom he doated on with all that affection which a man feels, who [-,-] in the decline of life, having few affections, clings more earnestly to those that remain.

Context after (unchanged): Cursed, cursed be the fiend that brought misery on his grey hairs, and doomed him to waste in wretchedness!

result.rationale: Replaces 'his niece' with 'his Elizabeth', naming her personally and dropping the kinship term; the relationship shifts from a family-role description to an individual bond. The comma removal is a minor punctuation change.
